The CAVE nodes, wired the way references exist for.

*Exported from Coda.*

```{r setup}
# install.packages(c("arrow", "reticulate", "dplyr"))
# remotes::install_github("natverse/fafbseg")  # not on CRAN
# fafbseg drives Python's caveclient through reticulate. Once per machine, run
# fafbseg::simple_python(); if a chunk below fails, fafbseg::dr_fafbseg() says why.
# The CAVE token is read from ~/.cloudvolume/secrets, as caveclient does in Python.

library(fafbseg)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r coda-helpers}
# Helpers, generated by Coda. These are the parts of the workflow that have
# no equivalent in the packages this document attaches, written out here so
# it stands on its own.

coda_cave_dataset <- function(datastack, version, neuron_table = NULL, id_column = "pt_root_id",
                              annotation_table = NULL, ref_column = NULL,
                              system_column = NULL, value_column = NULL, labels = NULL) {
  # A CAVE datastack at one materialization, and the neuron table Coda labels it with.
  #
  # An environment -- this function's own frame, which already holds every argument -- so
  # the neuron table (coda_cave_labels) is built once and shared by every chunk that reads it.
  # `labels` is passed in when an annotation source was wired to the Dataset on the canvas,
  # and replaces the datastack's own.
  version <- as.integer(version)
  environment()
}

.coda_cave_clients <- new.env()

coda_cave_client <- function(ds) {
  # caveclient's CAVEclient pinned to the dataset's materialization, so its timestamp is the
  # snapshot's: what Update root IDs brings ids forward to, and what listings describe. One
  # per datastack and materialization for the session, however many chunks name them.
  key <- paste(ds$datastack, ds$version)
  if (is.null(.coda_cave_clients[[key]])) {
    caveclient <- reticulate::import("caveclient")
    .coda_cave_clients[[key]] <- caveclient$CAVEclient(ds$datastack, version = ds$version)
  }
  .coda_cave_clients[[key]]
}

coda_cave_query <- function(ds, table, ..., limit = NULL) {
  # Rows of a table or view at the dataset's materialization, through fafbseg, with every
  # integer64 column -- an id -- as exact text, the form Coda keeps ids in.
  out <- fafbseg::flywire_cave_query(
    table, datastack_name = ds$datastack, version = ds$version,
    limit = limit, fetch_all_rows = is.null(limit), ...
  )
  for (name in names(out)) {
    if (inherits(out[[name]], "integer64")) out[[name]] <- as.character(out[[name]])
  }
  # Only the columns a plain list asked for: a bound point brings its supervoxel along
  # whatever `select_columns` names. A join's {table: columns} map is read as it comes.
  select <- list(...)$select_columns
  if (is.list(select) && is.null(names(select))) {
    out <- out[, intersect(unlist(select), names(out)), drop = FALSE]
  }
  out
}


#' Rename an annotation table's id column to `neuronId` and its cell type column to `type`.
coda_annotation_columns <- function(df, id_column) {
  if (id_column %in% names(df)) names(df)[names(df) == id_column] <- "neuronId"
  if (!("type" %in% names(df))) {
    for (name in c("cell_type", "celltype")) {
      if (name %in% names(df)) {
        names(df)[names(df) == name] <- "type"
        break
      }
    }
  }
  if (!("neuronId" %in% names(df))) return(df)
  ids <- as.character(df$neuronId)
  df$neuronId <- ids
  df[!is.na(ids) & ids != "", , drop = FALSE]
}


coda_cave_wide <- function(ds, table, kind_column, value_column, key, select, ...) {
  # One column per value of `kind_column`, each the first `value_column` per `key` -- an
  # annotation table read one kind at a time, as Coda does, since the whole of one can exceed
  # a deployment's row cap, which the server applies by truncating.
  client <- coda_cave_client(ds)
  kinds <- client$materialize$get_unique_string_values(table)[[kind_column]]
  wide <- NULL
  for (kind in unlist(kinds)) {
    rows <- coda_cave_query(
      # Through to caveclient as it is: fafbseg would read a kind like "1" in a
      # `filter_in_dict` as an id and send it as a number, which matches no string.
      ds, table, filter_equal_dict = stats::setNames(list(kind), kind_column),
      select_columns = select, ...
    )
    rows <- rows[!duplicated(rows[[key]]), , drop = FALSE]
    rows <- rows[, c(key, value_column), drop = FALSE]
    names(rows)[2] <- kind
    wide <- if (is.null(wide)) rows else dplyr::full_join(wide, rows, by = key)
  }
  wide
}

coda_cave_labels <- function(ds) {
  # Coda's neuron table for the datastack, one row per neuron and one column per annotation
  # kind, built on first use.
  if (!is.null(ds$labels)) return(ds$labels)
  if (is.null(ds$neuron_table)) {
    stop("This datastack publishes no neuron table, so the only list of its neurons is an ",
         "annotation source. Wire one to the Dataset on the canvas and export again.")
  }
  neurons <- coda_cave_query(
    ds, ds$neuron_table, select_columns = as.list(c("id", ds$id_column)),
    merge_reference = FALSE
  )
  out <- neurons
  if (!is.null(ds$annotation_table)) {
    wide <- coda_cave_wide(
      ds, ds$annotation_table, ds$system_column, ds$value_column, ds$ref_column,
      as.list(c(ds$ref_column, ds$value_column)), merge_reference = FALSE
    )
    if (!is.null(wide)) {
      names(wide)[names(wide) == ds$ref_column] <- "id"
      neurons$id <- as.character(neurons$id)
      wide$id <- as.character(wide$id)
      out <- dplyr::left_join(neurons, wide, by = "id")
    }
  }
  out$id <- NULL
  ds$labels <- coda_annotation_columns(out, ds$id_column)
  ds$labels
}


coda_cave_table <- function(ds, table, id_column = "pt_root_id", columns = NULL,
                            pivot_on = NULL, value_column = NULL) {
  # A CAVE annotation table as a Coda neuron table. A reference table has no root id of its
  # own -- it lives in the table it references -- so it is read through that join.
  client <- coda_cave_client(ds)
  reference <- client$materialize$get_table_metadata(table)$reference_table
  if (!is.null(reference) && !nzchar(reference)) reference <- NULL
  select <- function(own) {
    # A join needs a {table: columns} map naming both tables; a plain query needs a list.
    if (is.null(reference)) return(as.list(c(id_column, own)))
    stats::setNames(list(as.list(own), list(id_column)), c(table, reference))
  }
  if (!is.null(pivot_on)) {
    out <- coda_cave_wide(
      ds, table, pivot_on, value_column, id_column, select(value_column),
      merge_reference = !is.null(reference)
    )
    if (is.null(out)) out <- stats::setNames(data.frame(character(0)), id_column)
  } else {
    own <- columns
    if (!is.null(reference) && is.null(own)) {
      # A join must name its columns, so read one row to learn them.
      sample <- coda_cave_query(ds, table, limit = 1L, merge_reference = FALSE)
      own <- setdiff(names(sample), id_column)
    }
    out <- coda_cave_query(
      ds, table, select_columns = if (is.null(own)) NULL else select(own),
      merge_reference = !is.null(reference)
    )
    if (!is.null(own)) out <- out[, c(id_column, intersect(own, names(out))), drop = FALSE]
  }
  coda_annotation_columns(out, id_column)
}


coda_cave_table_info <- function(ds, table) {
  # Describe a table or view: print its metadata and row counts, and return its columns, each
  # with its R class and an example value from one row.
  client <- coda_cave_client(ds)
  views <- names(client$materialize$get_views())
  tables <- unlist(client$materialize$get_tables())
  if (!(table %in% c(tables, views))) {
    stop(sprintf('"%s" is not a table or view in this datastack. Available: %s',
                 table, paste(c(sort(tables), sort(views)), collapse = ", ")))
  }
  if (table %in% views) {
    meta <- client$materialize$get_view_metadata(table)
    cat(sprintf("%s  (view)\n", table))
    cat("  note: CAVE does not push a row limit into a view, so an aggregating one builds its",
        "whole result before handing back the single row read below.\n")
  } else {
    meta <- client$materialize$get_table_metadata(table)
    cat(sprintf("%s  (%s)\n", table, if (is.null(meta$schema_type)) "?" else meta$schema_type))
    # Two row counts that can differ by up to a third: the live table and the frozen snapshot.
    live <- client$annotation$get_annotation_count(table)
    frozen <- client$materialize$get_annotation_count(table)
    cat(sprintf("  rows: %s live, %s in v%d\n", format(live, big.mark = ","),
                format(frozen, big.mark = ","), ds$version))
    if (!is.null(meta$reference_table)) cat(sprintf("  annotates: %s\n", meta$reference_table))
    if (!is.null(meta$notice_text)) cat(sprintf("  NOTICE: %s\n", meta$notice_text))
  }
  if (!is.null(meta$description)) cat("\n", trimws(meta$description), "\n", sep = "")
  # split_positions gives separate x/y/z columns, matching the columns Coda lists.
  sample <- coda_cave_query(ds, table, limit = 1L, split_positions = TRUE)
  example <- function(x) {
    if (nrow(sample) == 0) return("")
    value <- x[[1]]
    if (length(value) == 1 && is.na(value)) "" else paste(format(value), collapse = " ")
  }
  data.frame(
    column = names(sample),
    type = vapply(sample, function(x) class(x)[1], ""),
    example = vapply(sample, example, ""),
    row.names = NULL
  )
}


coda_cave_tables <- function(ds, include_views = TRUE) {
  # The annotation tables in the dataset's materialization and, optionally, its views --
  # which hold a datastack's aggregations, FlyWire's connectivity among them.
  client <- coda_cave_client(ds)
  tables <- sort(unlist(client$materialize$get_tables()))
  out <- data.frame(table = tables, kind = rep("table", length(tables)))
  if (include_views) {
    views <- sort(names(client$materialize$get_views()))
    out <- rbind(out, data.frame(table = views, kind = rep("view", length(views))))
  }
  out
}


#' Combine two annotation tables: outer join on `neuronId`, the later table's values win.
coda_join_annotations <- function(left, right) {
  if (is.null(left)) return(right)
  if (is.null(right)) return(left)
  left <- left[!duplicated(left$neuronId), , drop = FALSE]
  right <- right[!duplicated(right$neuronId), , drop = FALSE]
  shared <- setdiff(intersect(names(right), names(left)), "neuronId")
  merged <- dplyr::full_join(left, right, by = "neuronId",
                             suffix = c("", ".coda_later"))
  for (name in shared) {
    later <- merged[[paste0(name, ".coda_later")]]
    take <- !is.na(later)
    merged[[name]][take] <- later[take]
    merged[[paste0(name, ".coda_later")]] <- NULL
  }
  merged
}


coda_search <- function(df, query) {
  # Filter rows with Coda's Explore Dataset search syntax.
  #
  # Terms are combined with AND; a leading "!" or "-" negates a term. A bare word matches
  # as a substring of the row's text. A term starting with "/" is a regex tested against
  # each field separately, so "/^LC4$" matches a field that is exactly LC4.
  # "field=value" compares one column; the other operators are > < >= <= != and ~ (regex).
  #
  # Differences from Coda: hits are returned in table order, not ranked by relevance,
  # and a query that matches nothing returns nothing (Coda retries it as a subsequence).
  ops <- c("==", "!=", ">=", "<=", "~", ">", "<", "=")
  tokens <- scan(text = query, what = "", quiet = TRUE)
  if (length(tokens) == 0) return(df)

  haystack <- NULL
  keep <- rep(TRUE, nrow(df))
  # Searchable columns: text columns plus neuronId, so "1200" finds a neuron id
  # but not a synapse count of 1200.
  search_cols <- names(df)[vapply(df, function(x) is.character(x) || is.factor(x), TRUE)]
  search_cols <- union(search_cols, intersect("neuronId", names(df)))

  for (raw in tokens) {
    negate <- FALSE
    if (nchar(raw) > 1 && substr(raw, 1, 1) %in% c("!", "-") &&
        !any(startsWith(substring(raw, 2), ops))) {
      # Only a leading ! or - with something after it negates.
      split_at <- regexpr(paste(ops, collapse = "|"), raw)
      if (split_at <= 1) { negate <- TRUE; raw <- substring(raw, 2) }
    }

    field <- NULL; op <- NULL; value <- NULL
    for (candidate in ops) {
      at <- regexpr(candidate, raw, fixed = TRUE)
      if (at > 1) {
        f <- substr(raw, 1, at - 1)
        if (grepl("^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*$", f)) {
          field <- f; op <- candidate
          value <- substring(raw, at + nchar(candidate))
          break
        }
      }
    }

    if (is.null(field)) {
      if (startsWith(raw, "/")) {
        # A bare regex (closing slash optional), tested against each field separately
        # so that anchors like "^LC4$" work.
        pattern <- substring(raw, 2)
        if (endsWith(pattern, "/") && !endsWith(pattern, "\\/")) {
          pattern <- substr(pattern, 1, nchar(pattern) - 1)
        }
        if (nchar(pattern) == 0) next
        mask <- rep(FALSE, nrow(df))
        for (col in search_cols) {
          # grepl returns FALSE for NA, so missing values never match.
          mask <- mask | grepl(pattern, df[[col]], ignore.case = TRUE)
        }
      } else {
        if (is.null(haystack)) {
          haystack <- tolower(do.call(paste, c(lapply(df[search_cols], function(x)
            ifelse(is.na(x), "", as.character(x))), sep = " ")))
        }
        mask <- grepl(tolower(raw), haystack, fixed = TRUE)
      }
    } else {
      if (nchar(value) == 0) next
      col <- names(df)[tolower(names(df)) == tolower(field)]
      if (length(col) == 0) { keep <- keep & FALSE; next }
      x <- df[[col[1]]]
      missing <- is.na(x)
      if (op == "~") {
        mask <- grepl(value, ifelse(missing, "", as.character(x))) & !missing
      } else if (is.numeric(x)) {
        right <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(value))
        cmp <- switch(op, "=" = , "==" = x == right, "!=" = x != right,
                      ">" = x > right, "<" = x < right, ">=" = x >= right, "<=" = x <= right)
        cmp[is.na(cmp)] <- FALSE
        # A missing value satisfies != and nothing else.
        mask <- if (op == "!=") cmp | missing else cmp & !missing
      } else {
        left <- tolower(ifelse(missing, "", as.character(x)))
        right <- tolower(value)
        cmp <- switch(op, "=" = , "==" = left == right, "!=" = left != right,
                      ">" = left > right, "<" = left < right, ">=" = left >= right,
                      "<=" = left <= right)
        cmp[is.na(cmp)] <- FALSE
        mask <- if (op == "!=") cmp | missing else cmp & !missing
      }
    }
    keep <- keep & (if (negate) !mask else mask)
  }

  df[keep, , drop = FALSE]
}


coda_synapses_between <- function(df, pre, post, position, confidence, location) {
  # Reshape a synapse-connection table into Coda's Synapses Between columns. `position` names
  # the drawn end's columns with {axis} for x, y and z.
  at <- function(axis) df[[sub("{axis}", axis, position, fixed = TRUE)]]
  tibble::tibble(
    neuronId = as.character(df[[pre]]),
    partnerId = as.character(df[[post]]),
    polarity = rep(location, nrow(df)),
    confidence = if (confidence %in% names(df)) as.numeric(df[[confidence]]) else NA_real_,
    x = as.numeric(at("x")),
    y = as.numeric(at("y")),
    z = as.numeric(at("z"))
  )
}


coda_update_root_ids <- function(ds, df, id_column = "neuronId", sample = NULL,
                                 supervoxel_column = NULL) {
  # Bring outdated root ids forward to the dataset's materialization, as Coda's Update root
  # IDs node: by each row's supervoxel where `supervoxel_column` is given, otherwise by the
  # majority of the old root's chunks (`sample` of them), adding `idConfidence`.
  #
  # Run as Python, with the notebook's own functions: the vote is int64 arithmetic, which R
  # has no exact type for, and the ids cross to Python and back as text.
  coda_cave_python()
  # Only the columns the repair reads cross to Python, as text; the rest of the table stays
  # in R, where the repaired ids (and, by majority, `idConfidence`) are written back into it.
  cols <- unique(c(id_column, supervoxel_column))
  asked <- as.data.frame(lapply(df[cols], as.character), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  names(asked) <- cols
  out <- reticulate::py$coda_update_root_ids_for_r(
    coda_cave_client(ds), reticulate::r_to_py(asked), id_column,
    sample = sample, supervoxel_column = supervoxel_column
  )
  df[[id_column]] <- out[[id_column]]
  if (is.null(supervoxel_column)) df$idConfidence <- out$idConfidence
  df
}

coda_cave_python <- function() {
  # Define the notebook's root-id functions in reticulate's Python, once per session.
  if (!reticulate::py_has_attr(reticulate::import_main(), "coda_update_root_ids_for_r")) {
    reticulate::py_run_string(CODA_CAVE_PYTHON)
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}

CODA_CAVE_PYTHON <- r"---(
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd


def coda_int64(values):
    """Convert a column of ids to exact int64; unreadable values become 0."""

    def one(value):
        try:
            # Exact for ints and decimal text of any length. pd.to_numeric is not: a single
            # null turns the column into float64, which rounds 18-digit root ids.
            return int(value)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            try:
                return int(float(value))
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                return 0

    return values.map(one).astype('int64')


def coda_stale_roots(client, ids):
    """Which rows hold a root id that is outdated at the client's timestamp."""
    askable = ids > 0
    stale = pd.Series(False, index=ids.index)
    if askable.any():
        latest = client.chunkedgraph.is_latest_roots(
            ids[askable].astype('int64').to_numpy(), timestamp=client.timestamp
        )
        stale.loc[askable] = ~np.asarray(latest, dtype=bool)
    return stale


def coda_write_roots(out, id_column, repaired):
    """Write repaired root ids into `out[id_column]`, keeping the column's dtype."""
    if repaired.empty:
        return
    if out[id_column].dtype == object:
        repaired = repaired.astype(str)
    else:
        # Keep the column's dtype so later comparisons and sorts behave the same.
        repaired = repaired.astype(out[id_column].dtype)
    out.loc[repaired.index, id_column] = repaired


def coda_update_root_ids(
    client, df, id_column='neuronId', supervoxel_column='supervoxel_id'
):
    """Update outdated root ids to this materialization, using their supervoxels."""
    out = df.copy()
    svids = coda_int64(out[supervoxel_column])
    # Look up new roots only for ids that are outdated at this materialization.
    stale = coda_stale_roots(client, coda_int64(out[id_column])) & (svids > 0)
    if not stale.any():
        return out
    roots = client.chunkedgraph.get_roots(
        svids[stale].astype('int64').to_numpy(), timestamp=client.timestamp
    )
    repaired = pd.Series(np.asarray(roots), index=out.index[stale])
    # Unknown supervoxels return root 0; skip those.
    coda_write_roots(out, id_column, repaired[repaired > 0])
    return out


def coda_update_root_ids_majority(
    client, df, sample, id_column='neuronId'
):
    """Update outdated root ids to this materialization by a majority of their chunks."""
    out = df.copy()
    ids = coda_int64(out[id_column])
    stale = coda_stale_roots(client, ids)
    confidence = pd.Series(np.where(ids > 0, 1.0, np.nan), index=out.index)
    confidence[stale] = np.nan
    if stale.any():
        # Each stale root's level-2 chunks, sorted and evenly strided down to `sample`.
        old = np.unique(ids[stale].astype('int64').to_numpy())
        owners, chunks = [], []
        for i in range(0, len(old), 50):
            # Fifty roots a request, as on the canvas, each reply cut to its sample at once.
            batch = old[i:i + 50]
            leaves = client.chunkedgraph.get_leaves_many(batch, stop_layer=2)
            for root in batch:
                c = np.sort(np.asarray(leaves.get(root, []), dtype='int64'))
                if len(c) > sample:
                    c = c[(np.arange(sample) * len(c)) // sample]
                owners.append(np.full(len(c), root, dtype='int64'))
                chunks.append(c)
        flat = np.concatenate(chunks)
        if len(flat):
            asked = np.unique(flat)
            placed = np.asarray(
                client.chunkedgraph.get_roots(asked, timestamp=client.timestamp)
            ).astype('int64')
            votes = pd.DataFrame({
                'old': np.concatenate(owners),
                'new': placed[np.searchsorted(asked, flat)],
            })
            # Unknown chunks (root 0) do not vote, nor do chunks placed in a root that is not
            # itself current, as a retired chunk can be. A tie goes to the lower id.
            candidates = np.unique(placed[placed > 0])
            current = candidates[np.asarray(client.chunkedgraph.is_latest_roots(
                candidates, timestamp=client.timestamp), dtype=bool)]
            votes = votes[votes['new'].isin(current)]
            tally = votes.groupby(['old', 'new']).size().rename('n').reset_index()
            tally['share'] = tally['n'] / tally.groupby('old')['n'].transform('sum')
            winners = (
                tally.sort_values(['old', 'n', 'new'], ascending=[True, False, True])
                .drop_duplicates('old')
                .set_index('old')
            )
            # Only the rows that found a winner: a NaN in the map would make the roots float64,
            # and an eighteen-digit id is not exact as a float.
            stale_ids = ids[stale].astype('int64')
            hit = stale_ids[stale_ids.isin(winners.index)]
            confidence[hit.index] = hit.map(winners['share'])
            coda_write_roots(out, id_column, hit.map(winners['new']))
    # Written over an existing column in its place, appended otherwise, as on the canvas.
    out['idConfidence'] = confidence
    return out


def coda_update_root_ids_for_r(client, df, id_column, sample=None, supervoxel_column=None):
    """Either method, with text handed back as plain strings: pandas may hold text as
    Arrow arrays, which reticulate does not convert into R."""
    if supervoxel_column is None:
        out = coda_update_root_ids_majority(client, df, int(sample), id_column)
    else:
        out = coda_update_root_ids(client, df, id_column, supervoxel_column)
    text = [c for c in out.columns if pd.api.types.is_string_dtype(out[c])]
    return out.astype({c: object for c in text})
)---"
```

```{r banc-public-cave}
)
```

```{r list-cave-tables}
# ── List CAVE tables ──
# NOTE: The Dataset wired here only names a datastack, and its chunk comes
# after this one, so this chunk names the same datastack and materialization
# itself.
.cave <- coda_cave_dataset("flywire_fafb_public", 783)
list_cave_tables <- coda_cave_tables(.cave, include_views = TRUE)
```

```{r cave-table-info}
# ── CAVE table info ──
# NOTE: In Coda the card shows this table’s description and row counts. Here
# they are printed, and the chunk’s output is the list of columns.
.cave <- coda_cave_dataset("flywire_fafb_public", 783)
cave_table_info <- coda_cave_table_info(.cave, "nuclei_v1")
```

```{r cave-table-2}
# ── CAVE table ──
# NOTE: The Dataset wired here only names a datastack, and its chunk comes
# after this one, so this chunk names the same datastack and materialization
# itself.
.cave <- coda_cave_dataset("flywire_fafb_public", 783)
cave_table_2 <- coda_cave_table(
  .cave,
  "hierarchical_neuron_annotations",
  id_column = "target_id",
  pivot_on = "classification_system",
  value_column = "cell_type"
)
cave_table_2 <- coda_join_annotations(cave_table, cave_table_2)
```

```{r filter-table}
# ── Filter Table ──
filter_table <- cave_table_2 |> filter(!is.na(`type`) & `type` != "")
```

```{r update-root-ids}
# ── Update root IDs ──
# NOTE: The Dataset wired here only names a datastack, and its chunk comes
# after this one, so this chunk names the same datastack and materialization
# itself.
.repair_at <- coda_cave_dataset("flywire_fafb_public", 783)
update_root_ids <- coda_update_root_ids(
  .repair_at,
  filter_table,
  id_column = "neuronId",
  supervoxel_column = "supervoxel_id"
)
```

```{r update-root-ids-2}
# ── Update root IDs ──
# NOTE: The Dataset wired here only names a datastack, and its chunk comes
# after this one, so this chunk names the same datastack and materialization
# itself.
.repair_at <- coda_cave_dataset("flywire_fafb_public", 783)
update_root_ids_2 <- coda_update_root_ids(
  .repair_at,
  filter_table,
  id_column = "neuronId",
  sample = 100
)
```

```{r flywire-fafb-public-cave}
# ── FlyWire FAFB public (CAVE) ──
# NOTE: Annotations are wired to this dataset in Coda, so they replace the
# datastack's own labels entirely.
flywire_fafb_public_cave <- coda_cave_dataset(
  "flywire_fafb_public",
  783,
  labels = update_root_ids
)
```

```{r table-df}
# ── Table ──
table_df_out <- update_root_ids
table_df_filtered <- table_df_out
table_df_out
```

```{r find-neurons}
# ── Find Neurons ──
# NOTE: A CAVE datastack has no server-side neuron query, so this reads the
# whole neuron index once and filters it here, as Coda does. Explore Dataset
# uses the same table.
find_neurons <- coda_cave_labels(flywire_fafb_public_cave)
find_neurons <- find_neurons |> filter(!is.na(.data[["type"]]) & grepl("^(?:LC.*)$", as.character(.data[["type"]]), ignore.case = FALSE, perl = TRUE))
```

```{r dataset-summary}
# ── Dataset Summary ──
# TODO: "Dataset Summary" is wired to a CAVE dataset, but its R chunk has
# only been written for neuPrint. The dataset is bound above, so fill this
# step in by hand.
```

```{r explore-dataset}
# ── Explore Dataset ──
# NOTE: Explore Dataset searches the whole neuron table locally. This is the
# datastack’s neuron table joined to its annotations (or to whatever is
# wired into the Dataset node’s `Annotations` port), fetched the first time
# anything needs it. On FlyWire that is 139,255 rows and takes a few
# seconds.
explore_dataset_all <- coda_cave_labels(flywire_fafb_public_cave)

explore_dataset_hits <- coda_search(explore_dataset_all, "side=left")

explore_dataset_selected <- explore_dataset_all |> filter(neuronId %in% c("720575940628857210"))
```

```{r synapses-between}
# ── Synapses Between ──
synapses_between <- coda_cave_query(
  flywire_fafb_public_cave,
  "valid_synapses_nt_v2_view",
  filter_in_dict = list(pre_pt_root_id = as.list(find_neurons$neuronId), post_pt_root_id = as.list(find_neurons$neuronId)),
  filter_greater_equal_dict = list(cleft_score = 50),
  desired_resolution = c(1, 1, 1),
  split_positions = TRUE
)
synapses_between <- coda_synapses_between(
  synapses_between,
  "pre_pt_root_id",
  "post_pt_root_id",
  "pre_pt_position_{axis}",
  "cleft_score",
  "pre"
)
# NOTE: This table names the two bodies of each synapse but not their cell
# types, which the canvas fills in from the dataset. Join them from a neuron
# table if you need them.
```

```{r synapses-between-2}
# ── Synapses Between ──
# NOTE: Coda has no entry for this datastack, so the synapse table name is
# read from its info record, as the canvas does.
synapses_between_2 <- coda_cave_query(
  custom_cave,
  coda_cave_client(custom_cave)$info$get_datastack_info()$synapse_table,
  filter_in_dict = list(pre_pt_root_id = as.list(find_neurons$neuronId), post_pt_root_id = as.list(find_neurons$neuronId)),
  desired_resolution = c(1, 1, 1),
  split_positions = TRUE
)
synapses_between_2 <- coda_synapses_between(
  synapses_between_2,
  "pre_pt_root_id",
  "post_pt_root_id",
  "post_pt_position_{axis}",
  NA_character_,
  "post"
)
# NOTE: This synapse table has no score column, so `Min confidence` (2) is
# ignored here and on the canvas.
# NOTE: This table names the two bodies of each synapse but not their cell
# types, which the canvas fills in from the dataset. Join them from a neuron
# table if you need them.
```

```{r synapses-between-3}
# ── Synapses Between ──
synapses_between_3 <- coda_cave_query(
  flywire_fafb_public_cave,
  "valid_synapses_nt_v2_view",
  filter_in_dict = list(pre_pt_root_id = as.list(find_neurons$neuronId)),
  desired_resolution = c(1, 1, 1),
  split_positions = TRUE
)
synapses_between_3 <- coda_synapses_between(
  synapses_between_3,
  "pre_pt_root_id",
  "post_pt_root_id",
  "pre_pt_position_{axis}",
  "cleft_score",
  "pre"
)
synapses_between_3 <- synapses_between_3[synapses_between_3[["partnerId"]] %in% coda_cave_labels(flywire_fafb_public_cave)$neuronId, ]
# NOTE: This table names the two bodies of each synapse but not their cell
# types, which the canvas fills in from the dataset. Join them from a neuron
# table if you need them.
```
